method: Whole reads with SHA256 and Git blob verification; extracted original buffered reader compiled with stub buffer/queue infrastructure and no-op readahead/logging.
findings: Header documents bytes_to_read=0 as whole-file read. Buffered reader sets bytes_remaining=0 and requests fread length0, then reports success because remaining is0.
Extracted-function reproduction on9-byte input: zero_to_eof success=1 read=0 submitted=0. Positive control explicit_length success=1 read=9 submitted=9.
Unbuffered path also initializes remaining to0 and clamps physical read count to remaining. Static analysis indicates zero-byte digest admission there; not independently executed.
Reader returns success separately from digest finalization, so consumers must preserve read outcome. No file identity or mutation snapshot validation is performed in these two files.

cache_quota_bytes is stored here but buffer semaphore budget is derived from thread count and buffer count; this module alone does not enforce advertised byte quota. Paranoid mode has no semaphore here; downstream digest implementation remains to inspect.

Thread-pool allocation checks and decrement are separate atomic operations; concurrent task creation needs examination. free(wait=false) with active tasks requires caller lifecycle discipline; no blanket runtime defect claim.
limits: Focused extracted original-function control only; not complete original rmlint build, end-to-end duplicate scan or performance benchmark.
No rrrah implementation change or fresh rrrah tests in this increment. Native pHash remains deferred.
